roleTitle: Site Reliability Engineer, Digital Content Platform
jobDescription: The digital content platform serves articles and video to a publisher's apps and websites. The Site Reliability Engineer owns the platform's reliability programme end-to-end, holds the production change approval for the content delivery services, leads the weekly reliability review, and is accountable to the head of engineering for the platform's availability targets. The platform serves several million readers a day through the publisher's apps and websites, and the role works with the product, engineering and editorial technology teams.
requirements: Owns the reliability programme end-to-end and holds production change approval for the content delivery services.
Builds and maintains the observability stack, alerting rules and runbooks for the content delivery services.
Leads the weekly reliability review and the incident postmortems and records decisions.
Coordinates availability targets with the product and engineering teams and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents known limitations and hand-over conditions for each reliability change.

evidence.text: Owned the reliability programme for the content delivery services for three years as the named owner in the engineering service catalogue, holding production change approval for those services and approving each change in the change tool under my own user id.
Built and maintained the observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry tracing), the alerting rules and the runbooks for the article and video delivery services.
Led the weekly reliability review and the incident postmortems, deciding the follow-up actions and their owners and recording the decisions in the reliability log.
Coordinated availability targets with the product and engineering teams, recording that product owned the target levels while I owned the error budgets, alerting and production change approval.
Responsibilities included programme ownership, production change approval, observability, runbooks and the reliability review for the content delivery services over about three years.

Work sample: the service catalogue entry naming the candidate as reliability owner, the change approval log for one quarter under the candidate's user id and one postmortem, with the change tool's identifiers as a verification trail.

Reference call with the former head of engineering: confirmed the candidate owned the reliability programme, held production change approval and led the reliability review; confirmed employment dates.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate is available for a technical session on the observability stack; notice period is two months.
